blocks.text: Placeholder text standing in for the article, so you can judge the reading experience rather than the news itself. Line length, spacing and letterforms are all real; the words are not.
Everything that normally surrounds a news page is gone here. No banner across the top, no video that starts on its own, no box asking you to subscribe, no list of stories from three years ago.

blocks.caption: A picture sits where it sat in the original article, with its own caption kept.

blocks.text: The headline, the byline, the pictures that belong to the story, and the text. Nothing moves unless you move it.
A paragraph at this width runs to roughly sixty-five characters, which is the range most people read comfortably.
Turning on bigger text keeps that proportion. The column does not grow with the type; the words per line drop instead, which is what you want when the letters get large.

items: Lists survive the stripping, because they carry meaning.
Navigation menus do not, because they do not.
Anything the extractor cannot identify is dropped rather than shown broken.

blocks.text: Short items are common in a feed like this. The layout should not look broken at three paragraphs, nor cramped at thirty.
